newsitem.title: USA: US June natgas prices gain on storage, temps--NGC.
newsitem.headline: US June natgas prices gain on storage, temps--NGC.

text.p: U.S. spot natural gas prices again registered a monthly gain for June, boosted by a steady stream of storage injections and increased power generation demand, Natural Gas Clearinghouse (NGC) said in its monthly survey.
U.S. spot gas prices for June averaged $2.16 per million British thermal units, up 18 cents from May's average of $1.98 and roughly even with last June's average, NGC said.
The largest monthly gains were in Louisiana, where prices on pipelines like Tennessee Gas rose 25 cents for the month to $2.25, still off five cents from year-ago levels.
Most Gulf pipes were up by 20 to 25 cents for the month and little changed from the same year-ago month.
Prices into Columbia Gas rose 20 cents from May to $2.25, still 10 cents below last year's levels, NGC said.
Prices on Oklahoma pipes were up by 15 to 20 cents, with ANR in Custer County quoted at $2.10, up from May's $1.90 and five cents above last year.

Prices represent NGC estimates of the median price for one month spot transactions at the indicated receipt points. The estimates are based upon quotes by industial end-users and local distribution companies, NGC said.
